concepts.prompt: Original production concept art for Wardenflame: Embers of the Vale. Grounded humane tactical fantasy, melancholy with warmth, restrained painted architectural reference for later pixel-art translation. Match reference image 1's Ashen Ford setting and old Warden masonry; reference image 2 establishes the approved Emberwick building materials and simple readable shapes. Use a 2:1 orthographic isometric camera, coherent top-left light, warm grey cut stone, cool stone shadows, weathered brown timber, muted ochre, repaired slate-grey shingles and restrained autumn colour. Clear separate material planes, no photographic microtexture, blur, bloom, text, lettering, labels, watermark, UI or copied franchise symbols. This is a modest practical cart bridge at a shallow ford, not a giant castle, rope suspension bridge, ruin or decorative walkway. Create a continuous low stone-and-timber bridge with old Warden stone abutments and two short stone-supported openings below a level timber deck. The usable road is two adult figures wide, broad enough for one small farm cart. Broad flat deck boards form an unbroken walking surface from approach to approach; load-bearing timber crossbeams sit on the stone piers. Low solid stone parapets border the deck without blocking the lane. At the far-bank landing place a single small Warden stone gatehouse with patched timber/slate roof BESIDE the lane, with a hinged timber road barrier attached at the entrance. No tower over the walking lane, roof over the deck, huge defensive walls or magical glow. The bridge deck, piers, parapets, gatehouse and removable barricades must read as separable buildable modules. Keep a narrow wadeable shallow-water strip beside the deck within the same ford, clearly distinct from dry planks; beyond this local crossing the river is deep and impassable. One modest neutral adult and one small empty handcart on the near approach establish scale, not characters or story outcomes. Show the entire structure and both bank contacts with generous margins on a neutral warm parchment field. The main view occupies the upper 75 percent; a small lower row gives a reverse isometric view and distinct construction studies of a pier, timber deck joint, parapet segment and gatehouse/barrier, all consistent with the main geometry. No second usable river crossing, town scene, distant northern ruins, heavy steam obscuring construction or painted grid. Proposed bank terrain is cold ash-grey on the burned side, worn brown track and restrained autumn grass on the town side, with crisp stones and small reed clumps; no orange/olive camouflage or snow. The Skarrow clan currently holds the bridge. Poor practical improvised defenses: patched brown hide screens tied to the outside of the parapet, rope-lashed sharpened stakes along the far approach verge, and a movable waist-high timber barricade across the far-bank lane entrance. Show the barricade as a removable object, not masonry sealing the bridge. A small exhausted camp is implied by one rolled hide and a cold cooking pot beside the gatehouse, not a crowded encampment. Keep the walking deck visible; no fire, battle, corpses, gore, monstrous trophies, skulls or luxury warlord decoration. The Warden stonework is old and sound underneath the makeshift defenses.

parameters.prompt: Create a revised production concept comparison sheet for Wardenflame. The previous state changes were much too subtle: the three states MUST read differently immediately as 200-pixel-wide thumbnails. Use reference image 1 ONLY as the fixed underlying architecture and restrained painted material style: the exact same low three-arched Warden stone bridge, continuous timber deck, stone parapets and small slate-roof gatehouse beside the far landing. Orthographic 2:1 isometric view, top-left light. Three equal LARGE separate panels from LEFT to RIGHT, same camera, same scale, same crop and same plain warm parchment background. Each panel shows the COMPLETE bridge and gatehouse with generous margins; eliminate scenic river valley, distant trees, tiny inset details, people and carts so the bridge occupies most of each panel. Narrow strip of water under the bridge only. No text, labels, frames, UI, symbols, letters or watermark. LEFT: SKARROW FORTIFIED. A conspicuous improvised checkpoint: tall ragged rusty-brown hide screens lashed to wooden posts along the far half of the parapets, well ABOVE parapet height; a broad dark timber spiked barricade visibly CLOSED ACROSS THE FAR LANDING road, waist to chest high; clusters of long sharpened stakes fanning out either side of the approach. One large patched dark brown hide awning projects from gatehouse side, visibly different in silhouette from the bare stone building. Preserve a visible broad clear deck before the closed checkpoint. Poor practical materials, not an evil skull fortress. MIDDLE: AFTER FORCE. The SAME stone bridge, piers, full safe timber walking deck and gatehouse. Every tall hide screen has been ripped down: exposed short snapped posts, no high screens. The barricade is visibly smashed into one large recognizable heap of crossbeams and broken stakes pushed fully off the road beside the gatehouse. The large side awning is collapsed into the debris; one torn dark hide hangs DOWN outside the parapet. The gatehouse roof edge and side wall carry a distinct localized charcoal-black scorch patch, no active fire; main roof structure remains intact. Clear uninterrupted cart lane across the entire bridge. No new buildings, missing parapets, broken load-bearing bridge, gore, bodies, victory banners or magical repairs. RIGHT: AFTER PARLEY AND THE HOTHEAD FIGHT. The SAME stone bridge, piers, unbroken deck and gatehouse, undamaged. The tall screens are removed and tied as bulky hide rolls LOW against the outside parapet. The two large timber checkpoint leaves stand OPEN and folded back along the banks, visibly upright, orderly and out of the lane. The big hide awning beside the gatehouse is re-tied into a neat pale tan shelter, with three modest tied grain sacks underneath; no overflowing harvest. Stakes neatly bundled on the verge, no broken pile, no scorch marks. Clear uninterrupted cart lane. The silhouette should read as an open staffed checkpoint or shared crossing without needing characters or text. Main architecture MUST stay identical across the three panels: same three arches, same deck length and width, same gatehouse location. Make the CLOSED SPIKED FORTIFICATION / SMASHED REMNANTS / ORDERLY OPEN GATE and PALE SIDE SHELTER large bold forms, not tiny dressing details. Strong readable material planes in warm grey stone, dark oak, slate and hide, restrained grounded humane tactical fantasy. Distinct states must survive downscaling; no fog, soft blur, cosmetic-only recolours or big surrounding landscape.
